subject: Activation gating: scheduled capacity reservation + redaction plugin for Zenith
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Activation gating: scheduled capacity reservation + redaction plugin for Zenith

Team —

Heads-up on Zenith Health: they verbally committed to a $1.6M ARR expansion contingent on a technical gating item in the SOW. Two asks coming from their infra and security teams that block signature: (1) the ability to reserve capacity for scheduled campaigns (they run predictable nightly inference windows for patient triage) so they can guarantee latency under load; (2) server-side PII redaction step configurable per-route before model tokenization (they cannot send raw PHI off their environment unless redacted).

Why this matters: legal is paused on the SOW until these are addressed. We have a 2-week window before they escalate to competitive procurement. Olson (Zenith CTO) said this is make-or-break.

Request: can Product/Eng scope a minimal, safe MVP we can promise in the SOW? My ask is a light commitment: a roadmap slot to deliver an API to create a time-windowed capacity reservation (start/end, capacity units), and a configurable redaction plugin that runs a set of regex/PII classifiers with opt-out flags for customers.

Constraints we can accept from Zenith: reservation can be best-effort with contractual SLA for availability during window (not full hard isolation), and redaction can be initially a hosted-managed config (no customer-provided models). We just need a clear deliverable, approximate ETA, and a risk call so I can update legal.

Attachments: SOW draft (attached), traffic pattern CSV (attached) — they included peak vs baseline.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

---
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Activation gating: scheduled capacity reservation + redaction plugin for Zenith

Kim —

Adding CS context: Zenith is running 8–9 batch windows nightly with spikes up to 3.6x baseline for a 30–45 minute period. They are worried about cold starts causing failed triage jobs and impacting patient flow. They prefer a model where we guarantee routing to warmed capacity during maintained windows.

For redaction: their security team will only accept server-side redaction; client-side is not allowed. They are open to us running a conservative PII blocker (redact email, SSNs, phone) in the path before the model.

I can share examples and coordinate a short call with their security folks if that helps.

—Monica
Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference

---
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Activation gating: scheduled capacity reservation + redaction plugin for Zenith

Thanks for the detail. High-level reaction from Eng: both asks are feasible but non-trivial. Quick notes: 

1) Scheduled capacity reservation: we can implement a reservation API that pins a % of pool capacity for named windows and routes traffic with a priority flag. Hard isolation (dedicated hardware) is expensive; for an MVP we propose a soft-reservation model: priority lanes + pre-warm orchestration that schedules warmup jobs 15–30 minutes before the window. That would reduce cold-starts significantly. Estimated scope: 6–8 sprints with one backend, one orchestration, and a small console UI. Risk: impacts autoscaler and scheduler complexity.

2) Server-side redaction plugin: we can ship an interceptor stage in the request pipeline that applies a configurable redaction step (regex + small model classifier). We should limit to deterministic patterns for MVP (SSN, DOB patterns, emails, phone numbers) and add a telemetry knob. Scope: 2–3 sprints. Risk: classifier false-positives may change output quality; need to include evals and a flag to bypass for vetted customers.

Questions for Sales/Legal: can the SOW accept an MVP definition that includes "soft reservations with pre-warm and priority routing" and a redaction feature "hosted-config redaction limited to deterministic patterns"? If yes, we can produce a timeline and resource ask.

—Dev
Engineering Lead, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

---
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 08:47:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Activation gating: scheduled capacity reservation + redaction plugin for Zenith

Operational note: if we go with soft-reservations, we need clear telemetry and an automatic fallback policy for when warm pools are depleted (fallback to best-effort with notification). Also think about quota accounting — reservations must be visible to billing to avoid overcommit. I recommend adding an initial Canary rollout (single region + limited capacity) for 2 weeks before broad activation.

I'll estimate infra work once Dev's timeline is firm.

—Markus
Staff SRE | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 4 Nov 2026 09:32:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Activation gating: scheduled capacity reservation + redaction plugin for Zenith

All —

I spoke to Zenith procurement this morning. They prefer contractual language that includes: a target ETA (not a precise date), a description of initial limitations (soft-reservation + limited redaction patterns), and canary acceptance criteria (sustained <10% error rate on redaction, 95th pct latency during windows under threshold). If Product/Eng can give an ETA range we can lock the SOW with conditional acceptance and a scoreboard for full delivery.

Proposed SOW language (draft): "Redwood will deliver an MVP scheduled capacity reservation API and a hosted redaction interceptor limited to deterministic PII patterns. The parties agree to a canary activation in a single region, and final production activation upon meeting acceptance criteria described in Attachment A."

If we can get an internal ETA by EOD, I can push legal for the conditional SOW.

—Marissa
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference

Thanks — that's helpful. Zenith needs an ETA and a short statement of limitations to avoid legal blocking. Dev/Markus: can you provide a rough ETA and a short bullet list we can paste into legal (3–4 lines) by tomorrow morning? If we can commit to an MVP canary in ~8–10 weeks and redaction in ~3–4 weeks, we can get a conditional signature and move ahead.

I'll schedule the legal/zenith call once we have the ETA so they see the internal alignment.

Kimberly Park
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
